# AutoHotkey v2.0.26 for Linux — linux.18

This technology-preview release turns the existing multi-client `ahk-inputd`
broker into an installable, opt-in, socket-activated system component and closes
several stream, hotplug and crash-recovery races found by new external oracles.

## Highlights

- Deb and RPM now ship `ahk-inputd`, `ahk-inputd.socket` and
  `ahk-inputd.service`; the generic tar installer offers
  `--inputd-service`. AppImage and Arch packages carry the daemon too.
- The system socket is `/run/ahk-inputd.sock`, owned by `root:input` with mode
  `0660`. Packages do not add users to `input` or auto-enable keyboard capture;
  both steps remain explicit administrator decisions.
- The daemon validates and inherits the standard `LISTEN_PID`/`LISTEN_FDS`
  socket, logs client PID/UID/GID from `SO_PEERCRED`, requires protocol HELLO,
  rejects mismatched versions and invalid rules, and supports fragmented and
  coalesced stream frames without blocking the evdev loop.
- Manual sockets now default to `0600`. Core auto-discovery checks the private
  `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and managed `/run` sockets only; `/tmp` is never trusted
  implicitly. `AHK_INPUTD_SOCKET` remains the explicit override.
- Polling uses stable device/client snapshots, fixing same-turn accept and sparse
  client-slot races. Device HUP/ERR/EOF now ungrabs, closes and prunes the dead
  fd so a hot-added replacement keyboard can be captured.
- The watchdog's signal handler uses only async-signal-safe closes and leaves the
  daemon permanently fail-open. Socket-activated daemons exit five seconds after
  the final client, releasing all keyboard grabs while the socket remains ready
  for demand restart.
- A live AHK process now retries a crashed broker every 500ms for up to five
  seconds, avoids competing in-process grabs during that window, reconnects to
  the restarted systemd service and re-subscribes rules without changing AHK PID.

## New independent evidence

- External `systemd-socket-activate`: inherited fd/path validation, fragmented
  HELLO, coalesced SUBSCRIBE/PING, protocol-order/version/rule rejection,
  `SO_PEERCRED` logs and externally owned socket preservation.
- Real systemd VM: first-connection start, SIGKILL restart with a new PID,
  five-second idle exit, demand restart, stable socket inode and full unit/socket
  cleanup.
- Installed deb + real `/usr/bin/ahk`: automatic `/run` discovery, broker mode,
  two demand starts, idle grab release (`GRAB_OK`) and apt-removal cleanup.
- Same-process recovery: one AHK PID fires an independent uinput F12 before and
  after the broker PID changes, proving reconnect and rule resubscription.
- Full root broker: distribution, replay, suppression, client-crash cleanup,
  real uinput hot-remove/hot-add, signal-safe watchdog fail-open and broker-death
  grab recovery.
- CI also gates the core S2C fragmented/coalesced parser, TSan, ASan,
  no-XWayland, four distro containers and release-package lifecycle.

## Important limits

- This remains a technology preview, not a claim of complete Win32 parity.
- Joining group `input` grants physical keyboard read access. Add only trusted
  automation users and require a complete logout/login after membership changes.
- Pure Wayland broker character streams still need a compositor layout source;
  hotkeys/custom combinations and suppression do not depend on that text source.
- libei/InputCapture, real Fcitx5 desktop, KDE and Flatpak host matrices retain
  their explicitly documented environment/upstream limits.
- The 24-hour soak remains cancelled by request. This release retains CI
  30-second and VM 5-minute evidence and makes no 24-hour claim.

## Enable the optional service

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now ahk-inputd.socket
sudo usermod -aG input "$USER"
# Log out completely and log back in.
AHK_INPUT_BACKEND=evdev ahk script.ahk
```

## Verification

```bash
sed -n 's/^  //p' CKSUMS.txt > checksums.sha256
sha256sum -c checksums.sha256

gh attestation verify <downloaded-file> \
  --repo MonoEven/Autohotkey_Linux
```

The Sigstore/GitHub attestation binds each digest to this repository, tag
workflow and commit. See `SECURITY.md`, `docs-v2/docs/howto/Install.htm` and
`docs-v2/docs/linux-port.htm` for the trust model, installation details and
capability boundaries.
